title: Jump Game
summary: Decide whether you can hop from the first index to the last.
statement: You start at index 0 of `nums`. Each `nums[i]` is the **maximum** jump length from index `i` (you may jump fewer steps). Return `true` if you can reach the last index, otherwise `false`.

examples.explanation: Jump 1 step to index 1, then 3 steps to the end.
Every path lands on index 3, whose jump length is 0.

hints: You don't need to try every sequence of jumps. As you move through the array from the left, what single number summarises everything the jumps so far make possible?

Greedy: keep the farthest index reachable so far. At each index i you can actually stand on (i <= farthest), update farthest = max(farthest, i + nums[i]). If you ever reach an index beyond farthest, you're stuck.

farthest = 0
for i from 0 to n - 1:
    if i > farthest: return false
    farthest = max(farthest, i + nums[i])
    if farthest >= n - 1: return true
return true

Exploring every jump sequence is exponential, and a DP over 'can I reach i' is O(n^2). The reachable indices always form a contiguous prefix [0, farthest], because from any reachable index you can also land on every index in between. So one number describes everything, and one left-to-right pass decides it: O(n) time, O(1) space. A single-element array is already at the last index, so it returns true.
